Judgment:

-
Challenge in this M.A.C.M.A. is to the award, dated 19.07.2016, in M.V.O.P.No.633 of 2013, on the file of the, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Judge for Trial of cases under S.Cs. & S.Ts (PoA)
Act) - cum - Additional District Judge, Vizianagaram (Tribunal for short), whereunder the Gurajapu Pydiraju vs Meesala Srinu 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137880442/

entities.text: Gurajapu Pydiraju vs Meesala Srinu 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Tribunal dealing with claim for compensation made by the claimant for a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- (at first Rs.2,50,000/- was claimed, subsequently it was enhanced to Rs.4,00,000/-), towards compensation, with regard to the injuries received by him, in a motor vehicle accident, which was occurred on 13.08.2011 at 09.00 a.m., awarded a sum of Rs.2,13,200/-.
2. The parties to this M.A.C.M.A. will hereinafter be referred to as described before the learned Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. The case of the claimant before the Tribunal, in brief, according to the averments set out in the Motor Vehicle accident claim, is that:
(i) The petitioner Gurajapu Pydiraju is a resident of Perapuram Village of Poosapatirega Mandal, Vizianagaram District.
He is doing milk business.
He used to earn Rs.300/- per day.
(ii) On 13.08.2011, at 09.00 a.m., petitioner along with his wife after visiting his wifes cousin at Mujeru Village, boarded an auto bearing No. AP 35 V 9384 (offending vehicle for short).

When the auto reached near Munjeru Village water tank, the respondent No.1 i.e., the driver of the auto drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and lost control over the auto and the auto turned turtle.
As a result, petitioner sustained injuries to his both legs, thighs and other injuries all over the body.

(iii) The petitioner was shifted to Community Health Centre, Bhogapuram, later to Government Head Quarters Hospital, Vizianagaram and later to Sri Sai Super Specialty Hospital, Vizianagaram, where the doctors took X-rays and found fractures to left femur and right femur and conducted surgery by fixing implants.

entities.text: Sri Sai Super Specialty Hospital, Vizianagaram
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner was treated as inpatient.
The doctor advised him for another surgery for removal of implants.
He spent huge amounts for treatment.
(iv) The Station House Officer, Bhogapuram police station, registered a case in Crime No. 186 of 2011 under Section 338 of IPC, against the respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 is the driver and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending auto.
Respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, all the respondents are jointly, severally responsible to pay compensation.

4. (i) Respondent No.2 got filed counter, which is adopted by the respondent No.1, denying the averments in the petition, contending in substance that there was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the respondent No.1 and the claim is tenable and it is excessive.
Respondent No.1 had valid driving license.
Claim is to be dismissed against respondent Nos.1 and 2.
The claim is to be honored by respondent No.3 only.
(ii) Respondent No.3 got filed counter, contending in substance that the claimant has to prove the manner of the accident and rash and negligent act alleged against the respondent No.1.

Respondent Gurajapu Pydiraju vs Meesala Srinu 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137880442/
2 No.1 had no valid driving license.

entities.text: Gurajapu Pydiraju vs Meesala Srinu 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accident occurred was due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the motorcyclist.
Hence, the claim is liable to be dismissed.
(iii) Respondent No.3 got filed additional counter contending that amount claimed highly excessive.

5. Basing on the above pleadings, the Tribunal settled the following issue for trial:
(1) Whether the respondent No.1 who is driver of offending vehicle auto bearing No.AP 35 V 9384 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident?
(2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and which respondents are laible to pay compensation amount?
(3) To what relief?
6.
During the course of trial, before the Tribunal, on behalf of the petitioners, PWs.1 and 2 were examined.
Exs. A1
to A7 were marked.

On behalf of the respondents,
respondent RWs.1 and 2 were examined.
Exs. B1 to B3 and Exs.X1 to X4 are marked.

7. The Tribunal on hearing both sides and on considering the oral as well as documentary evidence, answered the issues in favour of the claimant and against the respondents, awarded a sum of Rs.2,13,200/-, towards compensation.

8. Felt aggrieved that the compensation so awarded is not sufficient and reasonable,
the claimant, filed the present M.A.C.M.A.
9.

As against the findings of the Tribunal that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the respondent No.1 in driving the offending vehicle and that the respondent No.3/Insurance Company cannot escape its liability to pay compensation, there is no cross-objection or appeals.
Hence, the scope of this appeal is limited one.

10. Hence, the simple point for consideration is as follows:
"Whether the award, dated 19.07.2016, in M.V.O.P.No.633 of 2013, on the file of the,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Judge for Trial of cases under S.Cs. & S.Ts (PoA) Act ) - cum - Additional District Judge, Vizianagaram, in awarding a sum of Rs.2,13,200/- as against the original claim of Rs.4,00,000/-, is sustainable under law and facts and whether there are any grounds to interfere with the same?"
POINT:
Gurajapu Pydiraju vs Meesala Srinu 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137880442/
3 11.

entities.text: Gurajapu Pydiraju vs Meesala Srinu 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The contention of Sri Sai Narayana Rao, learned counsel for the appellant is that the Tribunal considered the disability as 10% as against the original disability of 50%,
for which a disability certificate was issued, as such, the compensation needs to be enhanced.

12. Sri Gudi Srinivasu, learned counsel for the respondent No.3, would contend that the by following the guidelines of the Honble Supreme Court, the Tribunal assessed the disability as that of 10%, which needs no interference.
13. The manner in which the claim was arrived at is disputed in the grounds of appeal.

According to the grounds of appeal, the income of the claimant is to be taken as Rs.300/-, per day and the Tribunal did not award extra nourishment and awarded meager amount for travelling and attendant charges and the Tribunal considered the disability as that of 10% as against 50%.
14. Firstly, this Court would like to deal with disability.

As evident from the evidence of PW.1 coupled with PW.2, who was the medical officer, the treatment that was given to PW.1 was regarding the fracture of right femur and left femur and a surgery was performed by fixing nails.
Ex.X1 is the case sheet.
Medical Board issued disability certificate, which is relating to due to mal-union and stiffness of right knee joint and patient has to go for another surgery.
It is to be noted that the Tribunal relied upon a decision of Honble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another1.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As seen from the above decision, a duty is cast upon the Tribunal, to consider the whole body disability and whether it is permanent or temporary.
As seen from Ex.A8, it is nothing but vague.
So, it is only relating to particular limb disability.
It is not a case of amputation and it is not a case of shortening of lower limb of the claimant.
So, the Tribunal rightly considered the disability as that of 10%.

15. With regard to the contention that the claimant was getting income of Rs.300/-,
per day.
It is not substantiated.
The Tribunal 2011 ACJ 1 rightly considered the notional income as Rs.4,000/-, per month and awarded loss of earnings for three (03) months @ Rs.4,000/- per month.

The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards transportation and attendant charges, which needs no interference.
However, the Tribunal did not award any amount under the head of extra-nourishment.

16. Having regard to the above, this Court is of the considered view that the amount of Rs.20,000/-, is reasonable towards extra- nourishment, because the petitioner lost his earnings for a period of three (03) months.
During the period of treatment and during post treatment, definitely the petitioner needs some special diet in terms of extra nourishment, so as to get faster recovery.

Except that, the award, dated 19.07.2016, in M.V.O.P.No.633 of 2013, on the file of the, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Special Judge for Trial of cases under S.Cs. & S.Ts (PoA) Act ) - cum - Additional District Judge, Vizianagaram, needs no interference.

Gurajapu Pydiraju vs Meesala Srinu 2 Others on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137880442/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The tribunal awarded compensation as follows:
Sl.

No . Name of the head under which Amount awarded in compensation is granted Rs.
1.

For two grievous injuries 70,000/-
2. For pain and suffering 20,000/-
3. For transportation and attendant 10,000/-
charges 4.

For loss of earnings 12,000/-
5.
For disability 81,600/-
6. For medical bills 4,600/-
7. For future surgery 15,000/-

Total: Rs.2,13,200/-
The above heads of compensation absolutely needs no interference.
So, an amount of Rs.20,000/-, is to be added to the heads of compensation, which is reasonable.

Hence, the total compensation the claimant is entitled to receive is Rs.2,33,200/-
(Rs.2,13,200/- + Rs.20,000/-).

Absolutely, except relating to the extra nourishment,
there are no merits in the appeal.

Hence, compensation is to be enhanced from that of Rs.2,13,200/- to Rs.2,33,200/-.
18.

In the result, the M.A.C.M.A. is allowed in part, by enhancing the compensation from Rs.2,13,200/- to Rs.2,33,200/-, with interest @7.5% per annum on the enhanced amount of Rs.20,000/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The respondents shall deposit the rest of the compensation, within a period of one month from the date of this judgment and on such deposit, the petitioner is at liberty to withdraw entire compensation.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE A.V. RAVINDRA BABU Dt.06.05.2024.
